source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: The correct order of steps for a system development life cycle is

options.A: Analysis, Planning, design, test, document, implement, evaluate.
options.B: Planning, Analysis, implement, design, document, test, evaluate.
options.C: Planning, Analysis, design, document, implement, test, evaluate.
options.D: Analysis, Planning, design, implement, evaluate, test, document.

explanation: SDLC begins with planning, then analysis and design; the design is documented, implemented (coded), tested and finally evaluated.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Translating a required task for system development into a series of commands that a computer will be able to understand is
explanation: Programming (coding) converts the design of a task into instructions the computer can execute.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Designers create system prototypes to

options.A: make the programmers understand how the system will function.
options.B: make the user visualize how the system will look like when it is developed and receive feedback
options.C: give a demo of the system to his administrating system manager to show as report
options.D: make both programmers and user understands how the system will look and function

explanation: A prototype lets users see and try a model of the future system early so their feedback can refine the requirements.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Dotted arrows in a DFD are used to represent
explanation: In real-time/extended DFD notation, solid arrows are data flows and dashed (dotted) arrows are control flows.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question:
A data dictionary has consolidated list of data required for
i. Documenting
ii. Input form designing
iii. Temporarily stored items
explanation: The data dictionary documents all data elements, flows and stores (including temporarily stored items) and is used when designing input forms.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question:
Hierarchy of maintenance requests is in order
i. maintenance controller
ii. system supervisor
iii. change control authority

options.D: maintenance is not possible in this way

explanation: Per Pressman, maintenance requests go to the maintenance controller, who forwards them to a system supervisor for evaluation, and the change control authority finally decides on the action.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: The data which is eligible for record keeping during maintenance

options.A: source statements added by the program change
options.C: number of processing failures associated with the runs

explanation: Maintenance records (Swanson's list) include statements added/deleted, machine instructions, processing failures and many other items, so all apply.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: In the model of total effort expended in maintenance M = a + K(b-c), a represents

options.C: complexity attributed to the lack of good design and documentation
options.D: measure of the familiarity with the software

explanation: In the Belady–Lehman model M = p + K e^(c−d), p is productive effort, K an empirical constant, c the complexity due to poor design/documentation and d the familiarity with the software.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Debugging is

options.B: creating the bugs in the program for testing
options.C: finding and correcting errors in the program code.

explanation: Debugging is locating and fixing the errors (bugs) found in program code.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question:
Match the following
1. Verification - K. checking whether the software meets the decided specification
2. Validation - L. converting logics into computer program
3. Testing - M. checking whether the software meets customer requirements
4. Coding - N. to check is the software is giving desired output for all inputs
explanation: Verification checks against the specification (K), validation against customer requirements (M), testing checks outputs for inputs (N), and coding converts logic into a program (L).

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which is not valid difference between verification and validation

options.A: Verification: Verification is carried out before the Validation. | Validation: Validation activity is carried out just after the Verification.
options.B: Verification: Testing like black box testing, white box testing and gray box testing are done under this. | Validation: Reviews, Meetings and Inspections are done under this.
options.C: Verification: Cost of errors caught in Verification is less than errors found in Validation. | Validation: Cost of errors caught in Validation is more than errors found in Verification
options.D: Verification: Execution of code is not comes under Verification. | Validation: Execution of code is comes under Validation.

explanation: It is reversed: reviews, meetings and inspections are verification (static) activities, while black/white/gray box testing is part of validation.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which statement is correct about of testing

options.A: It is done only for customer satisfaction that the product is working properly and is optional step.
options.B: It is a problem statement which lists specific inputs that are typically expected to be entered by the user and precise output values that a perfect program would return for those input values
options.C: It is finalized when the coding is completed

explanation: Testing is mandatory and continues beyond coding; a test case set lists the expected inputs and the precise outputs a correct program should produce.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question:
The primary objective of system implementation is
i. to build a system prototype
ii. to train users to operate the system
iii. to implement designed system using computers
iv. write programs, create databases and test with live data
explanation: Implementation turns the design into a working computer system: writing programs, creating databases and testing with live data. Prototyping belongs to analysis/design.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which design is perfect for long use, maintainability and up-gradation

options.C: design the system in independent modules
options.D: Create versions of the program frequently

explanation: Independent (loosely coupled) modules can be changed or upgraded individually, which makes the system maintainable over a long life.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question:
The system analyst is required to perform the task(s) include
i. defining and prioritizing information requirement of an organization
ii. gathering data, facts and opinions of users in an organization
iii. drawing up specifications of the system for an organization
iv. designing, coding and evaluating the system
explanation: The analyst defines requirements, gathers facts and draws up system specifications; coding is the programmer's job.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which of the following is not the primary design objective
explanation: Users do not read the code, so 'understandable code for user' is not a design objective; cost, reusability and security are.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: A system when made of several discrete components is called
explanation: A system built from separate, discrete components (modules) is modular.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which of the following is true for cohesion and coupling

options.A: Coupling taken place between multiple modules whereas cohesion is the strength of various elements inside a module
options.B: A good design must have very high cohesion
options.C: A good design must have very low coupling

explanation: Coupling is inter-module dependency and cohesion is intra-module strength; good design aims for high cohesion and low coupling.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which of the following is not advantage of structured design

options.B: Controls for upgrades are very easy and low cost
options.C: Early versions of design can give pre-review of system
options.D: Real life systems can be easily modeled

explanation: Easy modelling of real-life entities is an advantage of object-oriented design, not structured (function-oriented) design.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: In IPO charts P stands for
explanation: IPO = Input–Process–Output.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which is not a reason to consult user while designing of structured walk

options.A: Probability of success improves with involvement of user
options.B: Feedback is received which is very important
options.C: User and programmer can communicate to decide the price of the software
options.D: User can be trained and made understood about system

explanation: Users are involved in walkthroughs for feedback, training and better success, not to negotiate the software's price.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question:
The correct order of input form design stages is
i. Determining the contents of the input
ii. Choosing appropriate input device
iii. Identify the inputs required by the system
iv. Designing forms for input
explanation: First identify the required inputs, then decide their contents, choose the input device/medium and finally design the input forms.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: From the following which is not the activity of software maintenance

options.B: adaptive maintenance: modifies software to properly interface with a changing environment

explanation: The maintenance types are corrective, adaptive, perfective and preventive; reverse engineering is a re-engineering technique, not a maintenance category.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Correct order of stages of testing
explanation: Testing proceeds from unit to integration to system testing, regression after changes, and finally user acceptance testing.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Organizational chart is an example of
explanation: An organization chart is a hierarchy chart, like the hierarchy (VTOC) part of HIPO (Hierarchy plus Input-Process-Output).

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Structured charts are developed after
explanation: Structure charts are a design tool derived from the DFDs produced during requirement analysis.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Out of following which comes under requirement specification
explanation: Analysis models such as data flow models are part of the requirement specification.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: The model in which system development is broken down into a number of sequential sections or stages represented by boxes, with each stage being completed before work starts on the following one. The outputs from one stage are used as inputs to the next.
explanation: This describes the linear-sequential waterfall model.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: The spiral model is advantageous than waterfall model

options.A: When the requirements of the system are well understood by the users
options.B: When the requirements are not well formed or understood by the users
options.C: When the product comes after one stage easily
options.D: When all the functional requirements are available after requirement analysis

explanation: The iterative, risk-driven spiral model suits unclear or evolving requirements; waterfall needs well-understood requirements.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question:
Match the following
1. Backtracking Approach - a) Black box testing technique
2. Software Maturity index - b) White box testing technique
3. Equivalence Partitioning Testing - c) Debugging Technique
4. Control Structure Testing - d) Maintenance Metric
explanation: Backtracking is a debugging approach, SMI is a maintenance metric, equivalence partitioning is black-box and control structure testing is white-box.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Cost-Benefit Analysis is performed during
explanation: Cost-benefit analysis determines economic feasibility during the feasibility study.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Project risk factor is considered in
explanation: The spiral model explicitly includes risk analysis in every cycle.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: A software project classifies system entities, their activities and relationships. The classification and abstraction of system entities is important. .....................methodology most clearly shows the classification and abstraction of entities in the system
explanation: Classification and abstraction of entities is shown best by an object-oriented methodology, which is not listed.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: In unit testing, interface testing is performed to assess
explanation: Interface testing checks that information flows correctly into and out of the unit, i.e. its external behaviour; internal logic is covered by path testing. (Best available option.)

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which of following is NOT defined in a good software requirement specification (SRS) document
explanation: An SRS states what the system must do, not how; algorithms are design/implementation details.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question:
Match the following based on Design
i. Import Coupling - a. Nominal communication between modules
ii. Procedural call Coupling - b. Minimum communication between modules
iii. External Coupling - c. Declaration of a module in another module
iv. Low Coupling - d. Communication between internal modules & Collaborators
explanation: Import coupling = one module declared/imported in another; routine (procedure) call coupling = nominal communication; external coupling = communication with collaborating external components; low coupling = minimum communication.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which of the following is not regression test case?

options.A: A representative sample of tests that will exercise all software functions
options.B: Additional tests that focus on software functions that are likely to be affected by the change
options.C: Tests that focus on the software components that have been changed
options.D: Low-level components are combined into clusters that perform a specific software sub-function

explanation: Combining low-level components into clusters is the bottom-up integration testing strategy; the other three are Pressman's three classes of regression tests.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: After Development phase, a document is prepared
explanation: System specification comes from analysis and design specification from design; the document tied to the development (programming) phase is the program specification. (Ambiguous question; best available option.)

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: A diagram that shows the major subsystems in an object-oriented system is called a
explanation: Among the options, a component diagram shows the major physical subsystems/components of an OO system and their dependencies.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: During the planning phase of the system development life cycle (SDLC), the ____ helps to define the scope of the problem.

options.B: project evaluation and review technique (PERT) chart

explanation: A context diagram shows the system boundary and external entities, defining the scope.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Clients play what role in the development of a new system?
explanation: The client is the person or group that funds (pays for) the system; users define processes and the project manager plans and leads.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Questionnaires can be useful in information gathering when users ____.

options.B: need prompting to respond to questions
options.D: do not have time for interviews

explanation: Questionnaires reach many users in many locations cheaply where interviews are impractical.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: ____ requirements are based on the procedures and rules that the organization uses to run its business.
explanation: Functional requirements are the activities the system must perform, based on the organization's business procedures and rules.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: The first item to be reviewed during a structured walkthrough is the documentation that was developed as part of the ____ phase of the systems development life cycle (SDLC).
explanation: Walkthroughs begin by reviewing the analysis-phase documentation (requirements) before the design built on it.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Error report is an example of
explanation: An error report is produced by the system, so it is an output.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: An external entity in the system is

options.A: Unit outside the system and controllable by system analyst
options.B: External unit which will be designed
options.C: A unit which is not shown in DFD
options.D: A unit outside the system and works completely independent manner

explanation: External entities (sources/sinks) lie outside the system boundary and are not controlled or designed by the analyst, though they appear in the DFD.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: The controlling factor which does not governs the software maintainability

options.B: inefficient maintenance team taking much time

explanation: Maintainability is governed by product factors such as standard languages, documentation and test cases; an inefficient team is not one of them.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: The code used for the validation purpose is known
explanation: Self-checking codes include a check digit used to validate the code value.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Feasibility checking is the step performed

options.A: Before requirements specifications are drawn up
options.B: during the period when requirements specifications are drawn up
options.C: After all requirements specifications are drawn up

explanation: The feasibility study decides whether to proceed before detailed requirement specifications are drawn up.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: What is incorrect about DFDs

options.A: process models have as many level 1 diagrams as there are processes on the level 0 diagram
options.B: every process in the level 1 DFD would be decomposed into its own level 1 DFD
options.C: The purpose of the level 0 DFD is to show all the major high-level processes of the system and how they are interrelated
options.D: level 1 DFD shows how level 0 processes operates in greater detail

explanation: A process in a level 1 DFD is decomposed into a level 2 DFD, not another level 1 DFD.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Effective software project management focuses on four P's which are
explanation: Pressman's four P's are People, Product, Process and Project.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: The first step in project planning is to
explanation: Planning starts by establishing the objectives and scope of the project.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: The application of knowledge, skills, tools and techniques to project activities to meet the project requirements.
explanation: This is the PMBOK definition of project management.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which of the following is a tool of time management for software development
explanation: Network diagrams, Gantt charts and critical-path analysis are all scheduling tools.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question:
Match the project manager responsibilities with their tasks
i. interpersonal responsibilities - a. disseminating information about tasks to the project team
ii. informational responsibilities - b. allocating resources according to the project plan
iii. decisional responsibilities - c. leading the project team
explanation: Interpersonal = leading the team, informational = disseminating information, decisional = allocating resources.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: What information is not essentially required in a project progress report

options.A: Reporting period to which it refers
options.B: Days taken and cost to complete the report

explanation: A progress report states its period, authors and date; the effort spent writing the report itself is not needed.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which of following is not the aim of project progress report

options.A: Provide an overview of project's progress up to date
options.B: To keep it as a document for customer satisfaction
options.C: Ensure that the key stakeholders are regularly informed
options.D: Inform the key stakeholders about issues that require immediate action or resolution

explanation: Progress reports inform stakeholders and raise issues; they are not kept just for customer satisfaction.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Objectives of risk management do not include

options.A: Minimize the effort in software coding
options.B: Minimize adverse impacts to project scope, cost, and schedule
options.C: Maximize opportunities to improve the project's objectives with lower cost, shorter schedules, enhanced scope and higher quality

explanation: Risk management targets threats and opportunities to the project, not coding effort.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question:
Match the processes with their deliverables
i. Risk management planning - a. Prioritized list of risks classified as high, moderate, or low
ii. Risk identification - b. RMP document
iii. Qualitative risk analysis - c. Risk register
iv. Quantitative risk analysis - d. Numerical analysis of the project's likelihood of achieving its overall objectives
explanation: Planning produces the risk management plan, identification produces the risk register, qualitative analysis gives a prioritized list and quantitative analysis gives numerical probability of meeting objectives.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which of the following is not an information gathering technique for risk identification?
explanation: Brainstorming, interviewing, SWOT and Delphi are risk-identification techniques; a 'risk calculator' is not.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which is not a suitable difference in qualitative and quantitative risk analysis?

options.A: Qualitative analysis assesses the likelihood and impact of identified risks to determine whereas quantitative analysis is a way of numerically estimating the probability that a project will meet its cost and time objectives.
options.B: Quantitative risk analysis involves statistical techniques whereas qualitative analysis is found using impact matrix.
options.C: Qualitative risk analysis generally follows qualitative analysis.

explanation: The statement is wrong: quantitative risk analysis generally follows qualitative analysis.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which statement is false?

options.A: Organizations that achieve high levels of maturity in the people management area have a higher likelihood of implementing effective software engineering practices.
options.B: The software developer and analyst must meet to define product objectives and scope alone.
options.C: Without information of technical and management constraints, it is impossible to define accurate estimates of the cost and risk.
options.D: Umbrella activities are independent of any one framework activity and occur throughout the process

explanation: Objectives and scope must be defined together with the customer (stakeholders), not by developer and analyst alone.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which is not the meaning of W's W5HH

options.A: Why is the system being developed?
options.B: Who is responsible for a function?
options.C: What will be done, by when?
options.D: Where the organizational hierarchy plays its role?

explanation: Boehm's W5HH asks Why, What/When, Who, Where are they located organizationally, How and How much; 'where the organizational hierarchy plays its role' is not one of them.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Defect removal efficiency (DRE) can be computed as (where E represent effort and D represent defects)
explanation: DRE = E/(E + D), where E is errors found before delivery and D is defects found after delivery.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which is not a quality metric?
explanation: Pressman's quality measures are correctness, maintainability, integrity and usability.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which of the following condition if hold true suggests that process is out of control?

options.A: A single metrics value lies outside the upper natural process limit (UNPL)
options.B: Two out of three successive metrics values lie more than two standard deviations away from average metric value Am
options.C: All the metrics cannot be calculated together
options.D: Eight consecutive metrics values lie on one side of Am

explanation: A single value outside the UNPL is the first (primary) out-of-control rule. Note: per Pressman's zone rules, options B and D are also out-of-control conditions, so the question is ambiguous.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which is not a reusable software resource from the following
explanation: Pressman's reusable resources are off-the-shelf, full-experience, partial-experience and new components; environmental resources are a separate category.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which of the following is not a good and reliable cost and effort estimate

options.A: Delay estimation until late in the project
options.B: Ask from customer about his budget
options.C: Base estimates on similar projects that have already been completed
options.D: Use relatively simple decomposition techniques to generate project cost and effort estimates

explanation: Pressman's options for reliable estimates are delaying estimation, using similar past projects, decomposition and empirical models; the customer's budget is not an estimate.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question:
In a sample of empirical estimation model M represents
E = A + B x (M)^C
explanation: In E = A + B × (ev)^C, A, B, C are empirical constants, E is effort and ev (here M) is the estimation variable (LOC or FP).

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: COnstructive COst Model (COCOMO) model addresses
explanation: COCOMO II addresses the application composition, early design and post-architecture stage models; listed first is the application composition model. Note: options A, B and D are all correct, so the question is ambiguous.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question:
In the following effort estimation model, B represents
E = [LOC x B^0.333/K]^3 x (1/t^4)
explanation: In Putnam's software equation, B is a special skills factor, P (K here) is the productivity parameter and t is project duration.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Not a basic function of automated estimation
explanation: Automated estimation tools size deliverables, select activities and predict staffing, effort, cost and schedule, not maintenance plans.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which of the following is not a general risk component
explanation: Risk components (US Air Force) are performance, cost, support and schedule.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which of the following is not a common step to mitigate the risk

options.A: Train project teams so that they do not take risk
options.B: Meet with current staff to determine causes for turnover
options.C: Mitigate those causes that are under our control before the project starts
options.D: Once the project commences, assume turnover will occur and develop techniques to ensure continuity when people leave

explanation: B, C and D are Pressman's mitigation steps for staff turnover risk; training teams 'not to take risk' is not.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which of the following is not generally a reason for late project delivery

options.A: An unrealistic deadline established by someone outside the software development group and forced on managers and practitioner's within the group
options.B: Changing customer requirements that are not reflected in schedule changes
options.D: An honest underestimate of the amount of effort and/or the number ofresources that will be required to do the job

explanation: Pressman lists unrealistic deadlines, changing requirements and underestimates among causes of late delivery; payment release is not.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: ______________________is an activity that distributes estimated effort across the planned project duration by allocating the effort to specific software engineering tasks
explanation: This is Pressman's definition of software project scheduling.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Issues guiding software project scheduling
explanation: Scheduling principles include compartmentalization, interdependency, time allocation, effort validation, defined responsibilities, outcomes and milestones.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Reliable decomposition technique under software project estimation is
explanation: Decomposition techniques include software sizing, problem-based estimation (LOC/FP) and process-based estimation.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question:
The correct order of earned value calculation steps is
i. Estimate effort for work planned
ii. budgeted cost of work scheduled
iii. Estimate budget for work performed
explanation: First estimate effort for each planned task, sum them as BCWS, and then compute BCWP (budgeted cost of work performed).

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: The auditing and reporting functions of management are part of
explanation: Quality assurance consists of the auditing and reporting functions of management.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which of the following is not a fundamental source of change

options.A: New business or market conditions dictate changes in product requirements

explanation: Pressman's sources of change are new business/market conditions, new customer needs, reorganization or business growth/downsizing, and budget or schedule constraints.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: ________________combines procedures and tools to manage different up-gradations of configuration objects that are created during the software process
explanation: Version control manages the different versions of configuration objects.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which of the following risk is the failure of a purchased component to perform as expected?
explanation: Sommerville classifies an under-performing purchased component (e.g. a CASE tool) as a product risk.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Software interoperability is:

options.A: The ability of a software system to work on different hardware platforms
options.B: The ability of a software system to work under different operating systems
options.C: The ability of a software system to exchange information with other software systems and to use the exchanged information
options.D: The ability to replace a software system with another software system that has similar functionality

explanation: Interoperability is the ability to exchange and use information with other systems; A and B describe portability.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Cyclomatic Complexity is :
explanation: V(G) = number of predicate (decision) nodes + 1 = E − N + 2.

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Grade of a product

options.A: Means the same thing as quality
options.B: can be used interchangeably with quality
options.C: Is the level of product or service

explanation: Grade is a category or rank of products with the same use but different features; quality is how well requirements are met.

explanation: In the controlled centralized (CC) team, the team leader handles top-level problem solving and internal coordination.

question:
Associate Potential Risk Conditions Associated With Each Knowledge Area
i. Integration - a. Poor resource allocation
ii. Scope - b. Poor definition of scope
iii. Time - c. Early release of competitive products
iv. Cost - d. Inadequate productivity
explanation: In the standard risk-conditions table: integration—poor resource allocation; scope—poor definition of scope; time—schedule pressure such as early release of competing products; cost—inadequate productivity.

question: Which of the following term is best defined by the statement: "The underlying technology on which the system is built is superseded by new technology."?
explanation: Sommerville defines technology change as a business risk where the underlying technology is superseded.

question: Which is a project attribute?
explanation: Project attributes describe the project itself, such as its resources (people, tools, schedule); effort is the estimated output. (Ambiguous question; best available option.)

question: Which is not an umbrella activity under software Engineering?
explanation: Umbrella activities include project tracking, risk management, SQA, technical reviews, measurement, SCM, reusability management and work-product preparation; encryption is not.

options.C: Delivering a product which is developed iteratively

source_file: Question Paper for Analyst-Cum-Programmer - 2014 Paper - II
question: Which type of risk factor is most likely to cause problems for a software project which develops military software?
explanation: Military/defence projects are governed by heavy documentation standards, so excessive paperwork is the characteristic risk (Capers Jones).

question: ______________________is a technique used to show the effects of change of one or more variables on an outcome.
explanation: Sensitivity analysis varies inputs to see their effect on the outcome.

question: A _________ is developed using historical cost information that relates some software metric to the project cost
explanation: Algorithmic cost models (e.g. COCOMO) use historical data to relate a metric such as size to cost.
